sources.title: Synthesis of Cathode Material Li2FeTiO4 for Lithium-Ion Batteries by Sol–Gel Method

steps.details: First, citric acid was dissolved in anhydrous ethanol. Then, CH3COOLi-2H2O, FeCl2-4H2O, and Ti(OC4H9)4 were added at a molar ratio of 2.05.1:1, and homogenized by continuous stirring for 24 h at room temperature.
The gel was obtained by continued heating in a water bath at 65 °C for 5 h.
Dried in a vacuum drying oven at 120 °C for 24 h to obtain sample precursors.
The precursors were placed in a tube furnace under an Ar atmosphere and precalcined at 500 °C for 8 h.
The precursors were subjected to secondary calcination at several temperature ranges (600 °C, 700 °C, 800 °C) and fully milled.

drying_steps.details: The coated electrodes were dried at 80 °C for 12 h under vacuum
punched into disks with a diameter of 10 mm and further vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 6 h

extraction_notes: The precursor molar ratio is typed as '2.05.1:1' in Section 2.1, which is likely a typo for '2.05:1:1'. This raw value was preserved as requested.
In Section 2.1, 'CH3COOLi-2H2O' and 'FeCl2-4H2O' are written with hyphens instead of dots; these raw chemical formulas have been preserved.

There is a discrepancy in the description of the cycle test: Section 2.3 states cycling stability was evaluated at 1 C for 100 cycles, but the results (Table 1 and Fig 10b) indicate the 100-cycle stability test was performed at 0.1 C.
